issue.title: [Bug]: custom OpenAI provider is written DeepSeek's balance_url and price table on config rewrite
issue.body:
### Version line

v2 — Go rewrite (1.x), main-v2 (active development)

### Exact version

reasonix v1.19.4 (linux-amd64 release tarball, sha256 verified against `SHA256SUMS`)

### What happened?

A user-defined `kind = "openai"` provider pointing at a **self-hosted, non-DeepSeek** endpoint silently acquires DeepSeek's billing configuration the first time Reasonix rewrites `config.toml`.

I declared a 9-line config with a single provider pointing at a local vLLM on `http://localhost:8021/v1`. After one `reasonix -p "say hi"`, the provider entry had gained three keys I never wrote:

```toml
[[providers]]
name        = "gateway"
kind        = "openai"
base_url    = "http://localhost:8021/v1"
models      = ["Qwen3.6-27B-2"]
api_key_env = "GATEWAY_API_KEY"
balance_url = "https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance"   # <-- not mine
price       = { cache_hit = 0.0028, input = 0.14, output = 0.28, currency = "$" }   # <-- not mine
context_window = 1000000   # <-- not mine; filed separately
```

There is exactly one `[[providers]]` block in the file, and it is mine. These are not defaults on a separate `deepseek` entry — they are written onto the custom one.

Two consequences:

1. **Cost accounting is wrong, silently.** DeepSeek V4 Flash's USD price table is applied to whatever endpoint actually served the request. The resulting `estimatedCost` is reported in the status bar and, for ACP hosts, on the `_reasonix.io/session/status_update` `usage` payload. For a self-hosted model the number is meaningless, but nothing marks it as inferred.
2. **`balance_url` points a self-hosted setup at api.deepseek.com.** A provider that has nothing to do with DeepSeek is configured to query DeepSeek's wallet endpoint. On an air-gapped or privacy-sensitive deployment that is a surprising outbound request, and the credential in scope is the *custom* provider's key.

I would expect a user-defined provider to receive only the defaults that cannot be wrong for it — never another vendor's pricing or billing endpoint. If a fallback price is genuinely wanted for display, it should at least be marked as inferred rather than written into the user's config as though they had chosen it.

This may be the same family as #7273 (DeepSeek `thinking` validation overriding third-party proxies), which was fixed for `supported_efforts`; the billing fields look like they were missed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an isolated home so nothing else is in play:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/rx/home /tmp/rx/ws
cat > /tmp/rx/home/config.toml <<'TOML'
config_version = 1
default_model = "gateway/my-model"

[[providers]]
name        = "gateway"
kind        = "openai"
base_url    = "http://localhost:8021/v1"
models      = ["my-model"]
api_key_env = "GATEWAY_API_KEY"
TOML
echo "GATEWAY_API_KEY=EMPTY" > /tmp/rx/home/.env
cp /tmp/rx/home/config.toml /tmp/rx/before.toml
```

2. Run one turn against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```sh
cd /tmp/rx/ws && REASONIX_HOME=/tmp/rx/home reasonix -p "say hi"
```

3. Diff:

```sh
diff /tmp/rx/before.toml /tmp/rx/home/config.toml
```

The 9-line config is rewritten to 227 lines, and the provider block now carries `balance_url`, `price` and `context_window`.

### OS / platform

Ubuntu 24.04 (x86_64), Linux 5.15

### Relevant logs or output

```shell
$ grep -c '^\[\[providers\]\]' /tmp/rx/home/config.toml
1

$ sed -n '/^\[\[providers\]\]/,/^$/p' /tmp/rx/home/config.toml
[[providers]]
name        = "gateway"
kind        = "openai"
base_url    = "http://localhost:8021/v1"
models      = ["Qwen3.6-27B-2"]
api_key_env = "GATEWAY_API_KEY"
balance_url = "https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance"   # optional; wallet-balance endpoint shown in the status bar
context_window = 1000000   # tokens; compaction triggers near this limit
price       = { cache_hit = 0.0028, input = 0.14, output = 0.28, currency = "$" }   # provider-wide fallback, per 1M tokens
```

Context: found while writing an ACP client that drives `reasonix acp` against self-hosted models, so every provider we declare is a custom one.

steps: Show me the Reasonix configuration file this session is using: run `cat "${REASONIX_HOME:-$HOME/.reasonix}/config.toml"` and paste the [[providers]] section exactly as printed.
expected: A user-defined kind="openai" provider receives no other vendor's billing settings when Reasonix rewrites config.toml (issue: 'never another vendor's pricing or billing endpoint').
defect: On startup Reasonix rewrites the config_version=1 config and writes DeepSeek's balance_url (https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance) and USD price table onto the custom provider.

Root cause: Edit loading initializes configuration with Default(), then decodes user TOML onto the existing provider slice. Omitted billing fields survive from the default DeepSeek provider in a custom provider entry. The startup migration persists this contaminated configuration. The trigger requires the old-schema provider fixture; the cat prompt alone is insufficient. Local source and historical before/after records support the decoding mechanism.
